subject: Procurement kickoff: paper process and payout preference
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@acme-corp.com>, Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Procurement kickoff: paper process and payout preference

Hi Samir / Lisa —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on the scope and timelines. Quick recap + concrete next steps so procurement can run through the packet: 

What we covered
- Contract path: standard Redwood SaaS SOW + Master Services Agreement (we'll push draft if you want redlines)
- Procurement choices: PO (invoice + 30/45 day terms) vs. Corporate card (one-off low friction) vs. Cloud marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace)
- Vendor setup: W‑9 (US), banking details (ACH wiring or payment via card), and vendor portal option

Immediate asks for Acme procurement team
1) Confirm preferred payment path (PO or card) and desired payment terms (Net30/Net45)
2) If PO: please either route a purchase order or confirm the procurement contact to receive invoice and remit instructions
3) If card: share the internal card owner for billing and any single-invoice limits
4) If marketplace: tell us which marketplace account (AWS account id / marketplace email) and we can toggle that option on our side

Attachments included: redwood_vendor_packet_v1.pdf (vendor setup checklist + sample SOW), W-9_Acme_instructions.pdf (our example W-9 request).

Next steps from Redwood side
- I’ll drop the vendor packet into your procurement portal if you share the portal URL or will email the packet to procurement@acme-corp.com
- Rishi (cc’d) will confirm finance-side fields we need for ACH and tax handling

Target timeline: we can be ready to invoice within 3 business days of receiving completed packet and banking info. If you prefer marketplace, that usually adds ~7–10 business days for account link and billing setup.

I’m putting a short mutual action plan at the bottom of this thread — please reply inline with the payment path you prefer and who should own the PO/card paperwork.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments:
- redwood_vendor_packet_v1.pdf (31 KB) — vendor checklist, sample SOW, contact list
- W-9_Acme_instructions.pdf (12 KB) — form guidance and where to send completed W-9
From: Samir Rao <samir@acme-corp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Procurement kickoff: paper process and payout preference

Neha —

Thanks for the clear recap and the packet. A few questions from our end after reviewing: 

1) For PO flow: can Redwood accept our standard PO terms (we have a Data Processing Addendum and a 60-day invoice window in a couple of our templates)?
2) Marketplace: we prefer marketplace where possible, but need to confirm whether Redwood has listing on AWS Marketplace for the SKU we discussed. If not, card or PO are our fallback.
3) Banking: our treasury team prefers ACH. Can you confirm the exact fields Redwood needs (routing, account type, tax ID)?

I’m copying procurement@acme-corp.com — Maria will own the intake and get back with either the PO or the marketplace account info.

Regards,
Samir Rao
Director of Product & Procurement Liaison
Acme Corp

Thanks Samir — quick notes from finance: 

- We can accept PO with Net30 or Net45 depending on Acme's policy; 60 days is outside our standard but we can evaluate for enterprise deals if required (would need an approval path and updated payment schedule in the SOW).
- For ACH we need: beneficiary name, account number, routing number (ABA), account type (checking/savings), bank name, and tax ID (EIN).
- If you send a completed W-9, we can expedite vendor creation in our ERP. Otherwise, we’ll need a W-8 form for non-US entities.
- Marketplace (AWS) is available for some SKUs — Neha, I’ll confirm internal listing status and whether this contract SKU is published there.

I’ve attached a short vendor_setup_instructions.docx that lists required fields and sample metadata our ERP expects. If procurement wants to upload into a vendor portal, just share the portal URL and we’ll push the packet there.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments:
- vendor_setup_instructions.docx (8 KB)

Samir / Maria / Lisa —

Appreciate the quick replies. Proposed mutual action plan below so procurement can pick the fastest path: 

A) Fastest (1–3 business days): Corporate card
- Maria confirms card owner and single-invoice limit
- Redwood issues first invoice; payment via card clears immediately

B) Standard (3–7 business days): PO + ACH
- Maria / procurement uploads completed W-9 and the PO to procurement@acme-corp.com or into your vendor portal (share URL).
- Finance (Rishi) will create vendor record once W-9 + banking fields received; Redwood will invoice per PO terms.

C) Marketplace (7–14 business days): AWS Marketplace listing
- Maria provides AWS account ID or marketplace email; Redwood will validate listing and enable marketplace billing.

Action items (please reply with who will own each):
- Maria: confirm preferred path (Card / PO / Marketplace) and attach either the PO or AWS account id
- Samir / Lisa: confirm whether any specific legal clause requests (e.g., 60-day terms) we should route earlier to Legal
- Rishi: confirm if any exceptions needed for Net60 in the SOW (Rishi: can you flag the approval owner if needed?)

If helpful, I can send a DocuSign powerform for the initial SOW signature — link below. Once we have either a PO or card details we’ll trigger provisioning.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/3421

Thanks — I’ll check back Monday if I haven’t heard.

Neha
